verse_notes.note: Name 113 can be divided bhāvanā-gamyā 'attainable through contemplation' or bhāvanā-agamyā 'unattainable by imagining'; the letters are the same. Names 112–125 turn to Her as Śiva's consort and to devotion.
Bhavānī (112), Śāmbhavī (122), Śarvāṇī (124) and Śāṅkarī (126) are each formed from a name of Śiva: Bhava, Śambhu, Śarva, Śaṅkara.

Name 128 sādhvī is one name here; at 711–712 Bhāskararāya divides the same word into sādhu + ī. With nirādhārā (132) begins the long series of names of the attributeless Brahman, mostly built on nis 'without' (to 187).

The prefix nis takes its shape from the next sound: nir before vowels and voiced sounds (nirlepā), niṣ before k and p (niṣkalā); the meaning never changes. Name 137 is nirākārā with long ā (corrected).
Names 144, 148 and 149 (with nitya 'ever') recall the Vedāntic 'ever pure, awake and free'.

report.summary: Checked all 81 names of ślokas 41–50 against text.json: Bhavānī and the names of devotion, then the long series of nirguṇa names built on nis 'without' (132–187), whose every prefix form (nir, niṣ, niś, nis, niḥ, nī) is explained as sandhi, followed by the 'without X / destroyer of X' pairs. Main findings: 156 is nī-rāgā (nis + rāga 'passion'), not nīr + āgā 'sin'; 126 śāṅkarī (with vṛddhi) is 'consort of Śaṅkara', not 'giver of happiness'; 113's meaning ('unattainable') contradicted its split ('attainable') — both divisions are traditional, the gamyā reading is followed and the other recorded; 133 nirañjanā is 'stainless'. Two external sandhis join names (116–117, 154–155). No problem was found in the Sanskrit.
